A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Singular Value Ensemble (SVE) research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SVE experiments on vision, NLP, OOD detection, corruption robustness, computational cost, and ensemble-size and weight-diversity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds uncertainty-score evaluations, selective classification, initialization sensitivity, and layer-selection ablations.

M1.justification: The frozen singular vectors, perturbed singular values, non-negativity constraint, separate heads, and averaged cross-entropy objective remain. Section 4 of v2 explicitly specifies trainable per-member biases and their additive initialization noise, whereas v1 omits bias handling. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes the procedure or documents an existing implementation detail.

E1.justification: All datasets and original classification, OOD, and corruption scenarios are retained. Appendix A of v2 adds selective classification on CIFAR-100, introducing rejection of uncertain predictions as an additional task requirement. Entropy/MI rescoring otherwise uses the existing CIFAR-100/CIFAR-10 coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Evidential Deep Learning and its temperature-scaled variant on Flowers102; Table 3 adds C-LoRA on ARC-Easy. Existing comparators remain. The new appendix analyses compare SVE with Deep Ensemble without replacing the broader original comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds entropy/MI OOD scoring, selective accuracy at 90%, 80%, and 70% coverage, AURC, and initialization/layer-scope sweeps. Existing splits and training budgets are retained. Table 1 changes the Flowers102 and CIFAR-100 backbone labels from ViT-S/14 to ViT-S/16, matching v1's training details; this does not establish rerunning those experiments.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Appendix A directly examines epistemic disagreement and error rejection, Appendix C tests initialization scales from 0 to 0.1, and Appendix D tests whether attention or MLP layers suffice. The original ensemble-size, pretraining-scale, corruption, and singular-value-diversity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The three-seed, mean-plus-standard-deviation statement remains in the training appendix. New Appendix A explicitly identifies its results as single-run and cautions against direct comparison with Table 4's multi-seed averages. New ablation Tables 9–10 report point estimates without variability; no increase in runs for retained results is established.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and the ensemble-size ablation remain unchanged, but substantial results are added in Tables 6, 7, 9, and 10 and the new baseline rows. Examples include Flowers102 EDL accuracy/ECE of 80.4%/71.9%, falling to 4.8% ECE after temperature scaling, and equal MSP-based AURC of 0.028 for SVE and Deep Ensemble. These are additional findings, not demonstrated v1-to-v2 performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4 revises Equation 7's parameter-overhead derivation to count 9d bias entries alongside 6d singular values per transformer layer. The expression changes from (M−1)/(2d) to 5(M−1)/(4d) for biased architectures, while retaining the former expression for bias-free architectures. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: SVE obtains diverse ensembles through shared singular vectors, provides strong calibration with low parameter overhead, and works across vision/NLP backbones from 22M to 7B parameters. The revised title and wording do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of concentrated OOD disagreement, initialization-dependent diversity, and partial-layer efficiency, plus a limitation concerning inherited backbone biases and spurious correlations. Appendix A also claims MI becomes more informative for OOD detection, although Table 6 shows better SVE detection metrics with entropy, limiting support for that interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future-code-release promise with a stated implementation link. It specifies bias initialization, forward-pass clamp(min=0), and bias-aware parameter accounting. The main hyperparameter table, hardware description, and timing settings are retained; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked repository's availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds C-LoRA and EDL references and discussion, plus Depeweg, Hüllermeier, and Fort references supporting uncertainty decomposition and ensemble-diversity interpretation. The broader positioning remains. Publication updates to existing references and the corrected Brier attribution do not represent newly cited research.

P1.justification: The title, running headers, abstract wording, publication information, method explanation, and limitations are revised. New appendix sections are inserted while the original appendices remain identifiable as B, E, F, G, and H. The six-section main narrative and most existing prose are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6, 7, 9, and 10 and expands Tables 1 and 3 with baseline rows. Original appendix tables become Tables 8, 11, and 12, and figures and tables move with pagination. Existing experimental plots are retained, with the overall presentation style largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new uncertainty and rejection analyses directly strengthen evidence for the retained epistemic-uncertainty claim, while initialization/layer ablations, corrected parameter accounting, and implementation disclosures improve understanding and reproducibility. The gains are bounded: Appendix A uses one run, and its broad claim favoring MI for OOD detection is not supported by SVE's Table 6 comparison. Overall, v2 provides useful additional validation without substantially changing the original findings.
